question: How do you comp a hybrid AE/CSM who handles expansion in their book?
answer:
**Split comp: 60% new-customer AE commission rate, 40% expansion/retention CSM bonus.** E.g., $200k OTE AE + $80k retention pool (monthly basis). AE component stays traditional (5% on new ARR); CSM component is fixed monthly bonus on book health (net churn <5% = $100% of bonus; net churn 10% = 50%; churn >15% = $0). Prevents gaming: AE can't "oversell new," abandon book to degrade, collect commission. **Why Hybrid AE/CSM Roles Exist:** At $20M–$80M ARR, companies often blend responsibilities: 1. **Mid-market SaaS:** AE closes deal, then CSM handles first 90 days. Painful handoff, customer complains "AE ghosted me." Solution: Same person for first 18 months = smoother journey. 2. **Territory-based expansion:** AE owns Fortune 500 account ($100k ACV, 5–8 divisions). New customer in Q1; expansion in Q2–Q4. AE is better positioned to expand (knows stakeholders, context) than a CSM. 3. **Cost efficiency:** Hiring 10 AEs + 10 CSMs = $400k total comp. Hiring 10 hybrid AE/CSMs = $280k comp (less senior than pure AEs, more commission-focused than CSMs). **The Comp Problem:** If hybrid AE/CSM is paid purely as an AE (5% on all ARR, new + expansion): - They close $1M new deal in Jan, earn $50k commission - Customer doesn't renew in month 11 = customer becomes CSM's problem - Hybrid keeps the $50k, plus closes another $1M new customer - Result: Churn-positive customer book, high net negative ARR If paid purely as a CSM (fixed $150k salary, bonus on retention): - AE incentive disappears; they stop hunting new customers - Book stagnates - Company misses ARR growth targets **Solution: Dual-Rate Comp Structure** **Component 1: New-Customer AE Commission (60% of OTE)** Same as regular AE: 5% commission on new ARR. | New ARR Closed | Commission | |---|---| | $500k | $25k | | $1M | $50k | | $1.5M | $75k | Payable on new customer signature (month of close). **Component 2: Expansion + Retention CSM Bonus (40% of OTE)** Fixed monthly bonus pool, paid on book health metrics: | Metric | Target | Payout | |---|---|---| | Net Expansion Rate (NER) | >110% | $3.5k/mo | | Customer Churn Rate | <5% | $2k/mo | | Customer Health Score Improvement | >20% avg | $1k/mo | | **Total Monthly CSM Bonus** | All targets hit | **$6.5k/mo = $78k/yr** | **Full Comp Example:** - Base salary: $100k - AE commission (new): Target $50k (assuming $1M new ARR/year) - CSM bonus pool: $78k (monthly, assuming all targets hit) - **Total OTE: $228k** At 100% attainment: - Base: $100k - New AE commission: $50k (fixed based on 2025 average new sales) - CSM bonus: $78k (if NER/churn/health targets hit) - Total: $228k **Why This Prevents Gaming:** 1. **New customer commission is earned upfront:** Hybrid still gets paid for closing deals (new customer = $50k day 1). 2. **Expansion/retention is earned monthly:** If they ignore book, net churn goes negative, CSM bonus goes to $0. 3. **Example abuse scenario:** Hybrid closes $1M new customer with terrible onboarding (no kickoff call, no health check). Customer churn by month 11. - Hybrid keeps: $50k AE commission (earned at close) - Hybrid loses: $6.5k × 10 months = $65k in CSM bonus (book health deteriorated) - **Net hit: -$15k** (incentivized them to NOT abuse) **Measuring Book Health (The Hard Part):** **Metric 1: Net Expansion Rate (NER)** - Formula: (Beginning ARR + Expansion - Churn) ÷ Beginning ARR - Target: >110% (company grows from existing customers) - How hybrid influences: AE/CSM upsells new product lines, adds seats, upgrades tiers - Measured monthly, paid on 3-month rolling average (prevents month-to-month noise) **Metric 2: Churn Rate** - Formula: Annual churn from AE/CSM's book - Target: <5% - Why it matters: If book starts at $5M and loses $250k (5%), net = -$250k ARR loss, CSM bonus drops to 50% or $0 **Metric 3: Health Score Improvement** - Formula: % of customers in book moving from "At Risk" to "Healthy" status (tracked in Gainsight or HubSpot) - Target: 20%+ improvement quarter-over-quarter - How hybrid influences: regular check-ins, product training, ROI check-ins **Payout Gates (The Fairness Mechanism):** | Scenario | NER | Churn | Health | CSM Bonus Payout | |---|---|---|---|---| | Exceeds all targets | >120% | <3% | >25% | 120% of pool ($93.6k annual) | | Hits targets | 110%–120% | 3–5% | 15–25% | 100% of pool ($78k annual) | | Misses some targets | 100–110% | 5–10% | 10–15% | 50% of pool ($39k annual) | | Fails multiple targets | <100% | >10% | <10% | 0% (no CSM bonus) | **The Handoff Question:** At what point does hybrid AE/CSM hand off to dedicated CSM? **Answer:** Typically after month 18–24 if account is >$50k ARR and stable. Hybrid keeps 25% of CSM bonus on that account (residual incentive) but CSM takes over daily management. Hybrid focuses on next new customer. **Risk: Comp Burnout** Hybrid AE/CSM role is 30% harder than pure AE (you're on the hook for retention). Burnout at 36 months is common. Mitigations: 1. **No more than 8–10 active customer relationships per hybrid** (vs. 40+ for pure AE) 2. **Cap new customer quota at 2–3 per year** (vs. 8–10 for pure AE) 3. **Equity refresh:** 0.05–0.10% annual refresh to extend retention 4. **Promotion path:** Year 3 → move to VP Customer Success OR Principal AE (pure new business) ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Hybrid AE/CSM] --> B[Close New Customer] B --> C[Earn AE Commission: 5%] A --> D[Manage Book] D --> E[Monthly CSM Bonus] E --> F{NER >110%
